title: Soft-pin oscillation simulator — lab notes and ops checklist
content:
PURPOSE
This is a personal lab notebook / scratchpad for the 'soft-pin oscillation' experiment I sketched during the release sync. Goal: validate heuristics that prevent oscillatory pin/unpin behavior when multiple clients with different affinity compete over pinned versions during slow rollouts.

RATIONALE
We see intermittent oscillations where a model flip causes a small set of tenants to pin, traffic shifts, then telemetry triggers an automated unpin, then pin again → noisy churn. Hypothesis: a short, adaptive dampening window + microbatch warmup per-client reduces churn without delaying rollback significantly. Want a runnable playbook + quick simulator to exercise edge cases before trying in prod.

EXPERIMENT DESIGN (high level)
- Simulator will model N tenants (100–5k), each with: affinity score, request rate distribution, client-side SDK pin timeout (t_pin), and backend warmup sequence.
- Release plan: phased drip from 0% → 1% → 5% → 10% over 6 hours (fast test) or slower 12–24h for sensitive customers.
- Control: current pin/unpin rules. Variant: soft-pin with dampening and micro-warmup.
- Success criteria: 90% reduction in flip cycles per-tenant, 95th percentile tail latency stays within SLO, no significant increase in time-to-rollback when a severe regression is triggered.

SIMULATOR NOTES (to self)
- Inputs: tenant_count, mean_rps_per_tenant, affinity_distribution (beta), pin_threshold_confidence, dampening_window_ms, warmup_batch_sizes.
- Outputs: flips_per_tenant, mean_rollforward_time, rollback_latency, token_cost_delta, collateral_affected_tenants.
- Quick idea: simulate 'client jitter' (random reconnects) and 'telemetry lag' (5–90s) to stress TTL heuristics.

DAMPENING HEURISTIC — initial crude algorithm
- When a tenant signals 'pin candidate' (via SDK), tag it with timestamp t0.
- Soft-pin enters a pending state for dampening_window (default 120s). Within window, if traffic to pinned variant remains > X% of tenant's requests and errors < E, commit pin; else cancel.
- If commit occurs, start a 'lockout' window (default 900s) where auto-unpin is suppressed unless severe regression alert (P1).
- Unpin allowed if: error rate > 3x baseline AND rolling 5m error volume > 200 or explicit operator action.

MICROBATCH WARMUP SEQUENCE (per-tenant)
1) Send very small prefix-only warmup (batch size 1, 5 requests) to populate KV caches.
2) Ramp to batch size 4 for 30s.
3) If tail latency < threshold and error rate stable, allow full traffic fraction.

CHECKLIST — BEFORE TRYING IN STAGING
- [ ] Flesh out simulator inputs/outputs and add randomized seeds
- [ ] Implement dampening state machine in local dev branch (infra/scheduler layer)
- [ ] Create a small synthetic tenant set (50 tenants) and run 1000 trial simulations to gather distribution
- [ ] Add telemetry events/markers for t0, commit, lockout start/end, unpin triggers to event-schema repo
- [ ] Draft experiment JIRA with acceptance criteria and rollback playbook (RED-OPS-1423)

STAGING RUN (quick playbook)
- Canary cohort: 5 internal tenants (IDs: int-001..int-005) with high affinity and low noisiness
- Steps:
  1) Deploy variant to canary pool (tag vX+1) but do NOT enable auto-commit
  2) Run simulated warmup sequence manually for each canary tenant for 15m
  3) Turn on dampening pending state with window=120s, lockout=900s, pin_confidence=0.6
  4) Observe flips_per_tenant and tail latency for 60m
  5) If >2 flips observed across any canary tenant or tail latency increases >10% -> abort and rollback

SAFETY & ESCALATION
- Immediate abort triggers (auto-unpin override): sustained 5m error rate > 3x baseline OR any P0 customer complaint (pager).
- Manual operator commands:
  - Force pin: infractl pin --tenant <id> --model <version> --reason "test-commit"
  - Force unpin: infractl unpin --tenant <id> --reason "safety-rollback"
  - Drain canary pool: infractl drain --pool canary-vx+1
- Telemetry to watch live: reply_error_rate_5m, tail_latency_95, flips_last_1h, model_memory_pressure, kv_cache_miss_rate

ROLLOUT CONFIG SNIPPET (ops copy/paste)
- rollout: {
    mode: phased,
    cohorts: [0.01, 0.04, 0.05],
    interval_minutes: 60,
    dampening_window_s: 120,
    lockout_s: 900,
    pin_confidence: 0.6
  }
(Will convert to actual YAML in infra repo before staging run)

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODO (short list)
- What is a reasonable default pin_confidence for low-volume tenants where signal is sparse? (Maya to weigh in)
- How does soft-pin interact with per-tenant warm caches that are expensive to rebuild? Need cost estimate.
- Should SDK expose explicit 'pin-intent' API call to reduce reliance on heuristic detection?
- Operationally: how do we present 'lockout' windows in Console UI without confusing customers?

NEXT STEPS
- Build simulator prototype (python, Jupyter) and commit to repo under experiments/softpin-sim
- Sync with Maya and Eli for a 30m pairing session to define metrics instrumentation
- Put a small gating ticket in the release checklist so SRE/response team is notified on any staging run

NOTES TO SELF
- Keep experiment narrow, avoid mixing canary for performance regressions with this availability-driven test.
- If we see persistent oscillation even with 900s lockout, escalate to explore client SDK changes (explicit pin hold TTL).

END.
